question: Because autonomy is one of the four prima facie principles of bioethics, a competent adult patient's refusal of emergency life-saving treatment must always be respected, even if death will result.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is actually true. If a patient has decision-making capacity, their refusal — even of life-saving treatment — must be respected. Autonomy can override the doctor's beneficent intent. When autonomy is operative in a competent patient, it prevails over paternalistic beneficence.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A competent adult's informed refusal must be respected — autonomy overrides beneficence and non-maleficence when the patient has decision-making capacity. Overriding a competent refusal constitutes battery.
